correctness.rationale: For fixed n>=2 the damped discrete harmonic chain is exponentially stable (energy decay and nonvanishing boundary components of all stiffness eigenmodes). Its impulse kernels are L1 and have explicit linear-interpolation DC gains. Scaled resetting-wall increments vanish in fourth mean at fixed lags by Brownian increments on no-reset events and an eighth-moment/Hölder estimate on rare-reset events. Minkowski and dominated convergence prove joint L4 approximation to the two wall values. Exact independent Laplace characteristic functions and fourth cumulants then yield the rank-two covariance and sharp kurtosis trough. Equal complete wall autocovariances imply complete second-order matching with stationary Gaussian OU walls. All formulas reconstructed independently and the included checker passed 487 assertions; numerical examples alone are not the proof.

value.rationale: The precise finite-n stationary displacement profile is motivated by physically existing boundary-reset harmonic-chain experiments and corrects reliance on only velocity/current and two-time covariance data. It gives the full joint rare-reset distribution, rank-two collective spatial constraint, explicit fourth-cumulant tensor, universal 3/2 lower kurtosis bound and sharp spatial locus controlled only by reservoir noise-to-reset ratios. It quantifies an observable physical distinction from Gaussian OU walls that no second-order stationary experiment could resolve, and is a reusable benchmark for spatial measurements. The result is neither a one-parameter numerical table nor a nominal rescaling of the earlier single-particle velocity findings.
